name: Color Moments Statistical Profiling
description: Computes the core statistical characteristics of color distribution (Mean, Standard Deviation, and Skewness) known as 'Color Moments'. Real-world illumination creates distinct, physically bounded distributions of color across surfaces. AI generation models often exhibit subtle, systemic biases in their mathematical latent spaces, producing color distributions that wildly deviate from statistical biological norms (e.g., abnormally symmetric color variance or skewed saturation).
algorithm: First, Second, and Third Order Statistical RGB/HSV Moments
mechanism: The algorithm calculates three mathematically specific metrics for each color channel: The 1st Moment (Mean) captures the average color intensity; the 2nd Moment (Standard Deviation) measures contrast and color spread; the 3rd Moment (Skewness) measures the asymmetry of the color distribution. Authentic photographs possess a natural, chaotic skewness governed by environmental lighting physics, shadows, and occlusions. AI images, computationally constrained by their training data distributions and latent decoding algorithms, often synthesize 'perfectly' balanced colors possessing an unnaturally low skewness, or conversely, an erratic variance curve that exposes the absolute lack of a single, unified physical light source.
parameters: Color Channels: HSV highly preferred, Metrics Evaluated: Mean (Brightness bias), Standard Deviation (Contrast spread), Skewness (Photometric asymmetry)
accuracy: Low-to-Moderate (60-70%) - Primarily a foundational, supportive 'feature-extraction' metric rather than a standalone definitive forensic test.
source: Stricker & Orengo (1995) / Reinhard (2001) - Statistical Color Similarity & Transfer Physics
useCase: Employed as a lightweight, front-line statistical sieve to detect abnormal global color distribution anomalies, revealing the lack of natural lighting physics in AI-synthesized outputs.

references.title: Stricker, M.A., & Orengo, M. (1995). Similarity of Color Images. SPIE Storage and Retrieval for Image and Video Databases.
Reinhard, E. et al. (2001). Color Transfer Between Images. IEEE CG&A.

strengths:
• Extremely fast and lightweight, requiring incredibly few computational resources to process an entire high-resolution image simultaneously.
• Forms a highly robust foundational feature set for machine learning ensemble classifiers when combined with deeper spatial texture metrics.
• Highly invariant to scaling, rotation, and basic geometric transformations.
limitations:
• Lacks the necessary diagnostic severity and precision to confidently flag an image as AI-generated on its own (dismal standalone reliability).
• Highly susceptible to false positives when evaluating heavily color-graded cinematic photos, high-key studio setups, or any imagery with intentional human artistic color manipulation.
• Loses significant forensic efficacy on authentic images containing extreme physical lighting phenomena (e.g., silhouettes, harsh lens flares) which naturally entirely distort the expected statistical statistical moments.
